title: The two delivery paragraphs of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d1/2)
subtopic: Narcotic Schedule II prescriptions delivered out of the commonwealth
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d1/2) continues after its main paragraph with two further paragraphs. The first provides that NOTHING IN THE SUBSECTION SHALL BE INTERPRETED TO PROHIBIT A RETAIL PHARMACY OPERATING WITHIN THE COMMONWEALTH FROM FILLING PRESCRIPTIONS FOR A NARCOTIC SUBSTANCE CONTAINED IN SCHEDULE II TO RESIDENTS OF STATES OTHER THAN MAINE AND THE STATES CONTIGUOUS WITH THE COMMONWEALTH, PROVIDED THAT: (1) the pharmacy shall be licensed for retail by the commonwealth and, if applicable, registered with the appropriate regulatory authorities in the state from which the prescription is received and the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, as applicable, for the dispensing of controlled substances; (2) the prescription shall be filled by a pharmacist licensed and registered in the state from which the prescription originates, if that state requires such registration and licensing, and shall be written by a practitioner licensed and authorized to engage in prescriptive practice and registered in the same state or a contiguous state to where the prescription is to be delivered and registered under federal law to write prescriptions, or shall be written by a nurse practitioner or physician assistant authorized by the state of the prescription's origin to write it, licensed and registered in the same state or a contiguous state to where the prescription is to be delivered and registered under federal law to write prescriptions; (3) the prescription shall be RECEIVED by the retail pharmacy VIA MAIL OR COMMERCIAL CARRIER or through an equivalent electronic means as may be authorized by federal law; (4) the registered pharmacist filling it shall determine, in accordance with professional standards and personal judgment, that it is AUTHENTIC, VALID, LEGITIMATE AND LEGAL IN THE STATE FROM WHICH IT IS RECEIVED and SHALL VERIFY the prescription by telephonic or other means, a pharmacist shall not fill a prescription for which verification cannot be obtained, and any delivery of controlled substances to residents of another state shall be in FULL COMPLIANCE WITH ALL LAWS AND REGULATIONS OF THAT STATE relative to the issuance and filling of prescriptions; (5) the pharmacy shall comply with ALL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS OF THE STATE TO WHICH THE PRESCRIPTION IS DELIVERED, including but not limited to enrollment in and adherence to the rules, regulations and requirements of that state's prescription monitoring program or an equivalent program, where applicable; and (6) any substances delivered shall be DELIVERED VIA MAIL OR BY A COMMERCIAL CARRIER TO A VERIFIED ADDRESS IN THE STATE OF RESIDENCE of the person for whom the prescription was written and shall not enter into the hands of any person in the commonwealth not directly associated by employment or subcontract with the United States Postal Service or commercial carrier selected for the purpose. The second paragraph provides that NOTHING IN THE SUBSECTION SHALL PROHIBIT A RETAIL PHARMACY OPERATING WITHIN THE COMMONWEALTH FROM FILLING PRESCRIPTIONS FOR A NARCOTIC SUBSTANCE CONTAINED IN SCHEDULE II FOR PATIENTS ADMITTED TO A LONG-TERM CARE FACILITY IN MAINE OR A STATE CONTIGUOUS WITH THE COMMONWEALTH, PROVIDED THAT (i) the pharmacy is licensed for retail by the commonwealth and, if applicable, registered with the appropriate regulatory authorities in the state from which the prescription is received and the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, as applicable, for the dispensing of controlled substances; and (ii) the medications are DELIVERED DIRECTLY TO THE LONG-TERM CARE FACILITY BY A COURIER EMPLOYED OR CONTRACTED BY THE RETAIL PHARMACY. The main paragraph of the same subsection states that nothing in the section shall authorize a mail-order pharmacy.
exam_relevance: Tests that s. 18(d1/2) does not stop at its Maine-or-contiguous-state prescriber paragraph: a retail pharmacy in the commonwealth may fill narcotic Schedule II prescriptions for residents of other states, with mail or commercial-carrier delivery to a verified address in the patient's state of residence, and for long-term care patients in Maine or a contiguous state, with delivery by the pharmacy's own courier, each on the conditions its paragraph states.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d1/2), unnumbered paragraphs following the main paragraph

exceptions: Each paragraph speaks of a retail pharmacy operating within the commonwealth and licensed for retail by the commonwealth; the main paragraph of the subsection states that nothing in the section shall authorize a mail-order pharmacy.

Delivery under the first paragraph is by mail or commercial carrier to a verified address in the patient's state of residence; under the second, directly to the long-term care facility by a courier employed or contracted by the retail pharmacy.
common_confusions: Reading s. 18(d1/2) as reaching prescriptions from practitioners registered in Maine or a contiguous state and nothing else, and so missing the paragraph for residents of other states.
Treating the other-state paragraph as permitting any delivery method, when it requires mail or commercial-carrier delivery to a verified address in the patient's state of residence.

Overlooking the delivery state's own law on the issuance and filling of prescriptions and its reporting requirements, including its prescription monitoring program, which the paragraph states as conditions.
verification_notes: The two unnumbered paragraphs following the main paragraph of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d1/2) read in the current text on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
